subject: English 1st Paper (English For Today)
topic: Answering Questions from Poems in English for Today (Question No. 10: পাঠ্যবইয়ের নির্বাচিত কবিতা ও স্তবকভিত্তিক প্রশ্নোত্তর)

items.text:
10. Answer any five of the following questions from the poems in your textbook.

(a) In “A Little Plant”, where does the plant lie before it wakes?
(b) In “A Little Plant”, what do the sunshine and raindrops ask the plant to do?
(c) In “Ode on Solitude”, what is meant by a few paternal acres?
(d) In “Ode on Solitude”, how do trees help the contented person in different seasons?
(e) In “Something Told the Wild Geese”, why do the birds prepare to leave?
(f) What might the journey of the geese suggest about responding to change?
(g) In “The Children’s Songs”, what qualities do the children seek?
(h) What does “head, heart and hand” suggest in “The Children’s Songs”?
items.explanation:
Sample answers (other supported interpretations may be acceptable):
(a) It lies asleep inside a seed buried in the ground.
(b) They call the little plant to wake and grow towards the light.
(c) The phrase refers to a small piece of land inherited from one’s father.
(d) They offer shade in summer and wood for warmth in winter.
(e) They sense that cold weather is approaching and it is time to migrate.
(f) One possible interpretation is that it suggests noticing signs of change and preparing in time.
(g) They ask for guidance to become truthful, self-controlled and helpful.
(h) It suggests using thought, feeling and action together in service of the country.

items.text:
10. Answer any five of the following questions from the poems in your textbook.

(a) In “Oh, They Say”, what do the speaker’s grey hairs bring to mind?
(b) What contrast does “Oh, They Say” draw between possessions and human life?
(c) In “The Field of the Embroidered Quilt”, how does the quilt express emotion?
(d) Why does the woman want the quilt placed on her grave in “The Field of the Embroidered Quilt”?
(e) In “Green Escape”, what does the speaker seek away from streets and crowds?
(f) What natural sounds or sights does the speaker notice in “Green Escape”?
(g) In “Contemplation”, what can the speaker see from a high place in the tree?
(h) How might the title “Contemplation” relate to the speaker’s experience?
items.explanation:
Sample answers (other supported interpretations may be acceptable):
(a) They remind him that he is growing older and that life is temporary.
(b) It contrasts concern for a house and wealth with the short and uncertain nature of life.
(c) Its stitched patterns can be understood as carrying the maker’s memories, love and sorrow.
(d) She associates the quilt with her grief and hopes it will connect her sorrow with Rupai’s.
(e) The speaker seeks peace and closeness to nature away from busy urban life.
(f) The speaker notices bees and birds, and hears the wild swan across the marsh.
(g) The view includes fields, rivers, sheep and the roofs of the town.
(h) It suggests thoughtful reflection while looking out at the world from the tree.

10. Answer any five of the following questions from the poems in your textbook.

(a) In “Oh, They Say”, what do people say about Hason Raja’s house?
(b) In “The Field of the Embroidered Quilt”, what is the woman making?
(c) In “The Children’s Songs”, what are the children asking for in their prayer?
(d) In “A Little Plant”, what happens after the little plant hears nature’s call?
(e) In “Ode on Solitude”, what does the happy person receive from the land?
(f) In “Something Told the Wild Geese”, what do the birds sense despite the pleasant surroundings?
(g) In “Green Escape”, what contrast is suggested between the crowd and nature?
(h) In “Contemplation”, why does a high position in the tree matter to the speaker?
items.explanation:
Sample answers (other supported interpretations may be acceptable):
(a) They say that his house is not good.
(b) She is sewing an embroidered quilt.
(c) They ask for guidance to live truthfully, kindly and responsibly.
(d) It wakes and grows out of the seed towards the world outside.
(e) The land supplies necessities such as food and materials for clothing and shelter.
(f) They sense the approach of winter and the need to leave.
(g) The crowd suggests noise and busyness, while nature offers quiet and freedom.
(h) It allows the speaker to see a wide view and reflect on the world.

10. Answer any five of the following questions from the poems in your textbook.

(a) In “Oh, They Say”, why does the speaker think about how short life is?
(b) In “The Field of the Embroidered Quilt”, how does the woman use her sewing to communicate?
(c) In “The Children’s Songs”, what does the request for self-control suggest?
(d) In “A Little Plant”, how is the seed described in relation to the plant?
(e) In “Ode on Solitude”, what does the wish for a quiet life suggest about fame?
(f) In “Something Told the Wild Geese”, what makes the birds’ departure surprising?
(g) In “Green Escape”, what does the swan’s call add to the scene?
(h) In “Contemplation”, how does the view from the tree encourage reflection?
items.explanation:
Sample answers (other supported interpretations may be acceptable):
(a) The thought of ageing and death reminds him that life does not last forever.
(b) She stitches memories and feelings into the patterns of the quilt.
(c) It suggests that good conduct involves governing one’s own actions.
(d) The seed is the small sheltered place in which the plant first lies asleep.
(e) The speaker values peace and contentment more than public recognition.
(f) The surroundings still look pleasant, although the birds anticipate winter.
(g) It adds a striking sound to the speaker’s experience of the marsh.
(h) The wide view gives the speaker a chance to think about the world beyond the immediate surroundings.

10. Answer any five of the following questions from the poems in your textbook.

(a) In “Oh, They Say”, how do grey hairs affect the speaker’s thoughts?
(b) In “The Field of the Embroidered Quilt”, what does the request concerning the grave reveal?
(c) In “The Children’s Songs”, how is strength connected with helping others?
(d) In “A Little Plant”, how are sunshine and raindrops presented as if they were human?
(e) In “Ode on Solitude”, what does the speaker value besides material necessities?
(f) In “Something Told the Wild Geese”, what do the bright berries suggest about the landscape?
(g) In “Green Escape”, why might the speaker pay attention to small creatures?
(h) In “Contemplation”, what does the view suggest about the speaker’s curiosity?
items.explanation:
Sample answers (other supported interpretations may be acceptable):
(a) They make him aware that he is ageing and that life is temporary.
(b) It reveals the woman’s wish for her quilt, which holds her grief, to remain connected with her after death.
(c) The prayer suggests that strength should be used to support people in distress.
(d) They are given voices and speak to the sleeping plant.
(e) The speaker values health, peaceful rest and time for study.
(f) They suggest that the landscape still looks attractive before winter arrives.
(g) Their presence helps make the natural world vivid and peaceful to the speaker.
(h) The speaker is curious about the larger world visible from the tree.

items.text:
10. Answer any five of the following questions from the poems in your textbook.

(a) In “Oh, They Say”, how does the speaker’s view differ from concern about an impressive house?
(b) In “The Field of the Embroidered Quilt”, what relationship does the woman remember through her work?
(c) In “The Children’s Songs”, why do the children ask to be fair rather than act from fear or favour?
(d) In “A Little Plant”, what does the movement from seed to outside world suggest?
(e) In “Ode on Solitude”, why are shade and winter wood useful details?
(f) In “Something Told the Wild Geese”, what role does instinct seem to play?
(g) In “Green Escape”, how does the speaker’s attention shift?
(h) In “Contemplation”, what might the open view symbolise?
items.explanation:
Sample answers (other supported interpretations may be acceptable):
(a) He sees the shortness of life as more important than having a grand house.
(b) She remembers her bond with Rupai and expresses sorrow associated with it.
(c) They wish to act honestly and justly instead of being influenced by pressure or advantage.
(d) It suggests awakening and the beginning of growth.
(e) They show how nature can provide comfort in different seasons.
(f) It alerts the birds to leave before the conditions become harsh.
(g) The speaker turns away from crowded streets and attends to sights and sounds in nature.
(h) It can suggest freedom, possibility and a wider perspective.
